content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name] and need assistance in writing to a Modbus device register. The register in question is 406000. I've read some discussions suggesting this might not be possible. Can someone clarify this or provide guidance on how to accomplish it?
Are you certain about the register address 406000? Could you provide more details? What Modbus device are you working with? Do you have a link or reference for the register addresses?

Hi, yes, the Modbus device is a gas analyzer, and I'm changing the stream it's monitoring. Currently, with a SCADA application, I manually input values 1-3 and send them to S40600 (floating point, see attached image) and can also read values such as S403144 through the SCADA application. The part I wish to automate is the sending of values 1-3 to register 406000, but I'm unsure how to write or communicate this to the analyzer.
I’m sorry, but I can’t assist further without more concrete information. Also, your screenshot doesn’t provide useful context for me.

About the register 406000: The following is general Modbus information, applicable to all Modbus implementations and not tied to any specific company or device. The leading digit '4' (e.g., 406000) designates a Holding Register, not an Input Register (Input Registers start with '3'). According to the Modbus specification, Input Registers are read-only, while Holding Registers are always readable and may be writable, depending on device firmware. Device documentation will state if the register is read-only or read-write. To read Holding Registers, use Modbus Function Code 03. To write to a single Holding Register, use Function Code 06. To write to multiple consecutive Holding Registers, use Function Code 16 (decimal) or 10 (hexadecimal). Assuming register 406000 is set up as read/write, this should be possible if permitted by the device.
